output.brief:
The price rise is not the main driver of the extra cancellations. Accounts with no accounting connector, about 7,200 of them, barely changed (1.8% to 1.9%), whether repriced or on the Founders lock, and this holds at every seat size. The whole rise sits in Quillbook-connected accounts, whose churn roughly tripled (about 2% to 6%) whether repriced or locked. The bigger-increase-leaves-more pattern appears because larger accounts are more likely to use Quillbook. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices. 1,212 of 1,900 accounts were hit, and 34% of those have cancelled against 8% of unaffected accounts. These failures are logged as warnings, so the health panel never showed them. The 'price' answers in exit surveys are probably a stand-in for 'not worth it when invoices are wrong'. Tallymarsh numbers are tiny and within normal variation.

Next steps: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority, 3–4 weeks. Contact all Quillbook accounts, including those that cancelled, to correct invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold, because it protects customers' books. Don't roll back the price or start the Tallymarsh rebuild now. Review the Tallymarsh log cheaply first. Treat sync failures as high severity and fix the support response times. Confidence is fairly high.
